memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses said to the whole Israelite community, 'This is what the Lord has commanded: From what you have, take an offering for the Lord. Everyone who is willing is to bring to the Lord an offering of gold, silver and bronze; blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen; goat hair; ram skins dyed red and another type of durable leather; acacia wood.'" - Exod 35:4-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the phrase that governs everything: "Everyone who is willing."

No quota. No assessment of income. No public list of who gave what. God asked for an offering and then left the giving to the heart.

Think how remarkable that is. This is the same gold that had recently been melted into a calf. God could have demanded it as compensation. Instead He invites it as worship. Grace does not extract; it invites.

Notice also "from what you have." Nobody was asked to give what they did not possess. Some brought gold; some brought goat hair. Both were needed, and neither giver was ranked above the other.

That releases us from a lot of false guilt. God does not ask you for someone else's capacity. He asks for willingness with what is actually in your hands.

Paul says exactly this: each of you should give what you have decided in your heart to give, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver (2 Cor 9:7). And the widow who gave two small coins was commended above the wealthy (Mark 12:43-44), because God weighs the heart, not the amount.

What has He put in your hands?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you give out of willingness or obligation?
2. What has God actually placed in your hands to offer?
3. Do you compare your giving with others' rather than examining your own heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, take what I have and make my giving glad rather than grudging. Everything I hold came from You anyway. Amen.
